fact: The Ministry of Lands says the UgNLIS, rolled out nationally between February 2015 and February 2020, is a computerized system through 22 Ministry Zonal Offices that reduces the time to check, update and transfer land.
The Ministry of Lands says the UgNLIS is being enhanced under the NaLISEP project run from October 2023 to May 2024 by IGN FI with World Bank support.
The Ministry of Lands says the DeSINLISI national roll-out fully integrated land registration, land administration, surveying and mapping, physical planning and property valuation in the UgNLIS.

The Monitor reports that Uganda's digital land registration system, UgNLIS, is in service and processes transactions, with 12,748 registered transactions and thousands pending at the Jinja zonal office.
The Monitor quotes the Jinja Registrar of Titles saying digital mapping links titles to surveys, though physical verification is still needed where maps differ.

Uganda's Ministry of Finance reforms tracker, confirmed 11 August 2026, says the National Land Information System (UgNLIS) has been upgraded and is operational in 22 zonal offices, with expansion to all land offices in progress.
Lands Permanent Secretary Okalany said the digitalised system handles land acquisition, transfer, surveying and planning, with titles processed within ten days when documents are in order.
IGAD says Uganda's Land Information System is in service, interoperable with physical planning, land administration, valuation, surveys and mapping, and land registration.
IGAD says Uganda's Land Information System is interoperable with land valuation, surveys and mapping.
IGAD says Uganda's Land Information System integrates land records with taxation (Uganda Revenue Authority).

State Minister Obiga Kania said workflows have been developed to integrate customary ownership certificate records into the National Land Information System; no transactions processed in it are stated.
